question: Why do English speakers wear an apron when medieval cooks wore a napron?
answer: Because English heard the n as part of the article. It came from Old French naperon, a small cloth, kin to napkin, and Middle English said a napron. Spoken aloud, a napron and an apron sound identical, and in time the n migrated. Adder, once nadder, lost its n the same way.
move: What a listener hears decides where one word ends and the next begins.
